record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: For smooth Lebesgue-measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of the disk, let G be the set of maps f with λ_+(f,μ) = 0, equivalently zero metric entropy by the stated inequalities. Which of the two Baire alternatives holds: either G is a dense G_δ set, or there exists a nonempty C^∞-open set U on which every map has entropy bounded below by some δ > 0?

evidence.quote: 4.3 - One of the 2 exclusive possibilities is true by Baire category : a) The set G is a dense Gδ. b) There exists U⊂G∞ µ , a C∞ open set, U̸=∅, for every g∈U one has hµ(g)≥δ, for some δ >0. Question. Is a) or b) true ?

artifact.category_tag: Smooth ergodic theory / metric entropy genericity
artifact.status_search_result: Berger and Turaev (2017, published 2019) proved Herman's positive entropy conjecture: the identity of the disk can be $C^\infty$-perturbed to an area-preserving diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy, and more generally area-preserving diffeomorphisms with positive metric entropy form a $C^\infty$-dense set near any elliptic fixed point. This rules out alternative (a) (the zero-entropy set $G$ is not dense in $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty_\mu(D^2)$). However, this does not establish alternative (b), since a nonempty $C^\infty$-open set on which entropy is uniformly bounded below by some $\delta>0$ has not been exhibited. The full dichotomy thus appears not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Any area-preserving C^r-diffeomorphism of a two-dimensional surface displaying an elliptic fixed point can be C^r-perturbed to one exhibiting a chaotic island whose metric entropy is positive.
status_evidence.claim: Berger–Turaev show positive metric entropy is C^∞-dense near elliptic points, so the zero-entropy set is not dense; alternative (a) fails.

status_evidence.title: Berger and Turaev's Proof of Herman's Conjecture of Positive Entropy
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that smooth area-preserving diffeomorphisms with positive metric entropy can be found arbitrarily close to the identity on the disk.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms density of positive-entropy diffeomorphisms, contradicting density of G.

status_evidence.title: On mixing diffeomorphisms of the disc
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs C^∞ area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the disk with various ergodic properties.
status_evidence.claim: Related constructions in Diff^∞_μ(D^2) but do not produce a C^∞-open set of uniformly positive metric entropy.
